```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
'use strict';
var root=document.getElementById('bs1'); if(!root) return;
var $=function(id){ return root.querySelector('#'+id); };
var svg=$('bs1_svg');
var INK='#18202b', MUTED='#6b7684', FAINT='#c9d0d8', BLUE='#1f6feb', VIO='#6d28d9', SHADE='#eef3fb';
var p=2, ne=5, cont=[], knot=2, selL=null, selB=null;
var X0=66, X1=800;
var SUP={'-':'⁻','0':'⁰','1':'¹','2':'²','3':'³','4':'⁴'};
function sup(n){ return String(n).split('').map(function(c){ return SUP[c]||c; }).join(''); }
function Ck(c){ return 'C'+sup(c); }

/* ---- the two bases ---------------------------------------------------- */
function knots(){                       /* uniform elements; repeats lower continuity */
  var U=[],j,k;
  for(j=0;j<=p;j++) U.push(0);
  for(k=1;k<ne;k++) for(j=0;j<p-cont[k-1];j++) U.push(k);
  for(j=0;j<=p;j++) U.push(ne);
  return U;
}
function bspl(x,U){                     /* Cox-de Boor; x strictly inside an element */
  var n=U.length-1, N=[], i, d, a, b;
  for(i=0;i<n;i++) N.push(x>=U[i] && x<U[i+1] ? 1 : 0);
  for(d=1;d<=p;d++){
    var M=[];
    for(i=0;i<N.length-1;i++){
      a=U[i+d]>U[i]     ? (x-U[i])/(U[i+d]-U[i])*N[i]           : 0;
      b=U[i+d+1]>U[i+1] ? (U[i+d+1]-x)/(U[i+d+1]-U[i+1])*N[i+1] : 0;
      M.push(a+b);
    }
    N=M;
  }
  return N;
}
function lagLocal(a,t){                 /* degree-p Lagrange on [0,1], equally spaced */
  var v=1; for(var b=0;b<=p;b++) if(b!==a) v*=(t-b/p)/(a/p-b/p); return v;
}
/* value of basis function idx at x, evaluated inside element e */
function valL(idx,e,t){ var a=idx-e*p; return (a>=0 && a<=p) ? lagLocal(a,t) : 0; }
function valB(idx,e,t,U){ return bspl(e+t,U)[idx]||0; }

/* ---- drawing helpers --------------------------------------------------- */
function sx(x){ return X0+(X1-X0)*x/ne; }
function panelGeom(top){ return {top:top, main:top+50, mh:150, slope:top+50+150+30, sh:46}; }
var GL=panelGeom(4), GB=panelGeom(304);
var YMIN=-0.42, YMAX=1.12;
function sy(G,v){ return G.main+G.mh*(YMAX-v)/(YMAX-YMIN); }
function path(pts){ var d=''; for(var i=0;i<pts.length;i++) d+=(i?'L':'M')+pts[i][0].toFixed(1)+' '+pts[i][1].toFixed(1); return d; }
var NS=60, TS=[]; for(var s=0;s<=NS;s++) TS.push(1e-7+(1-2e-7)*s/NS);

/* one basis function, element by element, so a jump is drawn as a jump */
function curvePieces(G,val,idx){
  var out=[];
  for(var e=0;e<ne;e++){
    var pts=[], nz=false;
    for(var s=0;s<TS.length;s++){ var v=val(idx,e,TS[s]); if(Math.abs(v)>1e-12) nz=true;
      pts.push([sx(e+TS[s]), sy(G,v)]); }
    if(nz) out.push({e:e, pts:pts});
  }
  return out;
}
function slopePieces(val,idx){
  var h=1e-6, out=[], mx=0;
  for(var e=0;e<ne;e++){
    var vs=[], nz=false;
    for(var s=0;s<TS.length;s++){
      var t=Math.min(Math.max(TS[s],2*h),1-2*h);
      var d=(val(idx,e,t+h)-val(idx,e,t-h))/(2*h);
      if(Math.abs(val(idx,e,TS[s]))>1e-12 || Math.abs(d)>1e-9) nz=true;
      vs.push(d); mx=Math.max(mx,Math.abs(d));
    }
    if(nz) out.push({e:e, vs:vs});
  }
  return {pieces:out, mx:mx||1};
}
function supportOf(which,idx,U){
  if(which==='B') return [U[idx], U[idx+p+1]];
  if(idx%p===0) return [Math.max(0,idx/p-1), Math.min(ne,idx/p+1)];
  var e=Math.floor(idx/p); return [e,e+1];
}

function drawPanel(G,which,title,sub,nb,val,sel,U){
  var s='';
  s+='<text x="'+X0+'" y="'+(G.top+18)+'" font-size="17" fill="'+INK+'"><tspan font-weight="650">'+title+
     '</tspan><tspan dx="12" font-size="14" fill="'+MUTED+'">'+sub+'</tspan></text>';
  var sp=supportOf(which,sel,U);
  s+='<rect x="'+sx(sp[0])+'" y="'+G.main+'" width="'+(sx(sp[1])-sx(sp[0]))+'" height="'+G.mh+
     '" fill="'+SHADE+'"/>';
  s+='<line x1="'+X0+'" x2="'+X1+'" y1="'+sy(G,0)+'" y2="'+sy(G,0)+'" stroke="#9aa3ae"/>';
  s+='<line x1="'+X0+'" x2="'+X1+'" y1="'+sy(G,1)+'" y2="'+sy(G,1)+'" stroke="#eef0f3"/>';
  s+='<text x="'+(X0-8)+'" y="'+(sy(G,1)+4)+'" font-size="12.5" text-anchor="end" fill="'+MUTED+'">1</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+(X0-8)+'" y="'+(sy(G,0)+4)+'" font-size="12.5" text-anchor="end" fill="'+MUTED+'">0</text>';
  for(var k=0;k<=ne;k++)
    s+='<line x1="'+sx(k)+'" x2="'+sx(k)+'" y1="'+G.main+'" y2="'+(G.slope+G.sh)+'" stroke="#d6dbe2" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/>';
  var i,j,pc;
  for(i=0;i<nb;i++){                    /* every function, faint */
    pc=curvePieces(G,val,i);
    for(j=0;j<pc.length;j++)
      s+='<path d="'+path(pc[j].pts)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+FAINT+'" stroke-width="1.3"/>';
  }
  pc=curvePieces(G,val,sel);           /* the highlighted one */
  var col=(which==='L'?BLUE:VIO);
  for(j=0;j<pc.length;j++)
    s+='<path d="'+path(pc[j].pts)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="3.2" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
  s+=jumpMarks(G,val,sel,col,function(v){ return sy(G,v); });
  for(i=0;i<nb;i++){                    /* invisible fat strokes to click on */
    pc=curvePieces(G,val,i);
    for(j=0;j<pc.length;j++)
      s+='<path class="hit" data-w="'+which+'" data-i="'+i+'" d="'+path(pc[j].pts)+
         '" fill="none" stroke="transparent" stroke-width="13"/>';
  }
  /* the slope strip */
  var sl=slopePieces(val,sel), mid=G.slope+G.sh/2, sc=(G.sh/2-3)/sl.mx;
  s+='<text x="'+(X0-8)+'" y="'+(mid+4)+'" font-size="12.5" text-anchor="end" fill="'+MUTED+'">slope</text>';
  s+='<line x1="'+X0+'" x2="'+X1+'" y1="'+mid+'" y2="'+mid+'" stroke="#c9d0d8"/>';
  for(j=0;j<sl.pieces.length;j++){
    var P=sl.pieces[j], pts=[];
    for(var q=0;q<TS.length;q++) pts.push([sx(P.e+TS[q]), mid-sc*P.vs[q]]);
    s+='<path d="'+path(pts)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="2" opacity=".85"/>';
  }
  s+=slopeJumps(sl,col,mid,sc);
  return s;
}
/* open/filled dots wherever the highlighted function itself jumps */
function jumpMarks(G,val,idx,col,Y){
  var s='';
  for(var k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var l=val(idx,k-1,1-1e-9), r=val(idx,k,1e-9);
    if(Math.abs(l-r)>1e-6){
      s+='<line x1="'+sx(k)+'" x2="'+sx(k)+'" y1="'+Y(l)+'" y2="'+Y(r)+'" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-dasharray="2 3"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+sx(k)+'" cy="'+Y(l)+'" r="4" fill="#fff" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="2"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+sx(k)+'" cy="'+Y(r)+'" r="4" fill="'+col+'"/>';
    }
  }
  return s;
}
function slopeJumps(sl,col,mid,sc){
  var s='', byE={};
  for(var j=0;j<sl.pieces.length;j++) byE[sl.pieces[j].e]=sl.pieces[j].vs;
  for(var k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var a=byE[k-1], b=byE[k];
    var l=a?a[a.length-1]:0, r=b?b[0]:0;
    if((a||b) && Math.abs(l-r)>1e-3*sl.mx){
      s+='<line x1="'+sx(k)+'" x2="'+sx(k)+'" y1="'+(mid-sc*l)+'" y2="'+(mid-sc*r)+'" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-dasharray="2 3"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+sx(k)+'" cy="'+(mid-sc*l)+'" r="3.2" fill="#fff" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1.8"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+sx(k)+'" cy="'+(mid-sc*r)+'" r="3.2" fill="'+col+'"/>';
    }
  }
  return s;
}
/* the clickable boundaries on the B-spline axis, each with its own C^k */
function knotMarks(){
  var s='', y=sy(GB,0), yl=GB.main-8;
  for(var k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var on=(k===knot), c=cont[k-1], X=sx(k);
    s+='<g class="hit" data-k="'+k+'">';
    s+='<rect x="'+(X-17)+'" y="'+(yl-16)+'" width="34" height="'+(GB.slope+GB.sh-yl+18)+'" fill="transparent"/>';
    s+='<text x="'+X+'" y="'+yl+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="'+(on?700:500)+
       '" fill="'+(on?VIO:MUTED)+'">'+Ck(c)+'</text>';
    s+='<path d="M'+X+' '+(y-7)+'L'+(X+7)+' '+y+'L'+X+' '+(y+7)+'L'+(X-7)+' '+y+'Z" fill="'+(on?VIO:'#fff')+
       '" stroke="'+(on?VIO:'#8b95a2')+'" stroke-width="1.6"/>';
    s+='</g>';
  }
  return s;
}

function draw(){
  var U=knots(), nL=ne*p+1, nB=U.length-p-1;
  if(selL===null || selL>=nL) selL=p*Math.floor(ne/2);   /* a vertex function: its kink is the point */
  if(selB===null || selB>=nB) selB=Math.floor(nB/2);
  var s='';
  s+=drawPanel(GL,'L','Lagrange basis',nL+' functions · always C⁰ at element boundaries',nL,valL,selL,U);
  s+=drawPanel(GB,'B','B-spline basis',nB+' functions · continuity chosen at each boundary',nB,
               function(i,e,t){ return valB(i,e,t,U); },selB,U);
  s+=knotMarks();
  for(var k=0;k<=ne;k++)
    s+='<text x="'+sx(k)+'" y="'+(GB.slope+GB.sh+18)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" fill="'+MUTED+'">'+k+'</text>';
  svg.innerHTML=s;
  syncShapes(); drawMap();
  $('bs1_pv').textContent=p; $('bs1_ev').textContent=ne;
  $('bs1_kv').textContent='at x = '+knot+':  '+Ck(cont[knot-1]);
  $('bs1_dn').disabled=(cont[knot-1]<=-1); $('bs1_up').disabled=(cont[knot-1]>=p-1);
  var same=(nB===nL);
  $('bs1_cap').innerHTML='<b>'+nL+'</b> Lagrange functions against <b>'+nB+'</b> B-spline functions on the same '+ne+
    ' elements.'+(same?' With every boundary at C⁰ the two counts agree: the two bases describe the same set of'+
    ' functions, and on each element the B-splines are exactly the Bernstein polynomials.':'')+
    ' Click any curve to highlight it; the shaded band is where it is nonzero. Click a diamond to pick a boundary.';
}

/* ================= the same functions as a map into the plane ================
   x(xi) = sum_A N_A(xi) x_A.  The x_A are Lagrange nodes (the curve passes
   through them) or B-spline control points (the curve follows them).          */
var mapSvg=$('bs1_map'), Q=[], P=[], keyL='', keyB='', GHOST=true, drag=null;
var WX=[-1.3,1.3], WY=[-0.30,1.12], MS=150;          /* plane window, px per unit */
var PAN={L:{x0:14, title:'Lagrange: the curve passes through its nodes'},
         B:{x0:416, title:'B-spline: the curve follows its control points'}}, MT=44;
function target(s){ return [-Math.cos(Math.PI*s), 0.82*Math.sin(Math.PI*s)]; }   /* a smooth arch */
function toSvg(w,q){ return [PAN[w].x0+MS*(q[0]-WX[0]), MT+MS*(WY[1]-q[1])]; }
function toPlane(w,X,Y){ return [WX[0]+(X-PAN[w].x0)/MS, WY[1]-(Y-MT)/MS]; }
function grev(U,i){ var s=0; for(var k=1;k<=p;k++) s+=U[i+k]; return s/p; }
function buildL(){ Q=[]; for(var A=0;A<=ne*p;A++) Q.push(target(A/(ne*p))); }
function buildB(){ var U=knots(); P=[]; for(var i=0;i<U.length-p-1;i++) P.push(target(grev(U,i)/ne)); }
/* one point of each curve, inside element e */
function ptL(e,t){ var x=0,y=0; for(var a=0;a<=p;a++){ var v=lagLocal(a,t), q=Q[e*p+a]; x+=v*q[0]; y+=v*q[1]; } return [x,y]; }
function ptB(e,t,U){ var N=bspl(e+t,U), x=0, y=0;
  for(var i=0;i<N.length;i++) if(N[i]){ x+=N[i]*P[i][0]; y+=N[i]*P[i][1]; } return [x,y]; }
function atXi(f,xi){ var e=Math.min(ne-1,Math.floor(xi)); return f(e, Math.min(xi-e, 1-1e-12)); }

/* Lowering continuity is knot insertion: the curve does not move, it gains a
   control point.  (Boehm's algorithm.) */
function insertKnot(Uold,Pold,u){
  var k=-1,s=0,i; for(i=0;i<Uold.length-1;i++) if(Uold[i]<=u && u<Uold[i+1]) k=i;
  for(i=0;i<Uold.length;i++) if(Math.abs(Uold[i]-u)<1e-12) s++;
  var R=[];
  for(i=0;i<=Pold.length;i++){
    if(i<=k-p) R.push(Pold[i].slice());
    else if(i>=k-s+1) R.push(Pold[i-1].slice());
    else { var a=(u-Uold[i])/(Uold[i+p]-Uold[i]);
           R.push([(1-a)*Pold[i-1][0]+a*Pold[i][0], (1-a)*Pold[i-1][1]+a*Pold[i][1]]); }
  }
  return R;
}
/* Raising continuity cannot keep every curve, so take the closest smoother one
   (least squares on a dense sample of the old curve). */
function refit(Uold,Pold,Unew){
  var n=Unew.length-p-1, M=[], rhs=[[],[]], i, j, e, s;
  for(i=0;i<n;i++){ M.push(new Array(n).fill(0)); rhs[0].push(0); rhs[1].push(0); }
  var keepP=P; P=Pold;
  for(e=0;e<ne;e++) for(s=1;s<40;s++){
    var t=s/40, q=ptB(e,t,Uold), N=bspl(e+t,Unew);
    for(i=0;i<n;i++) if(N[i]){ rhs[0][i]+=N[i]*q[0]; rhs[1][i]+=N[i]*q[1];
      for(j=0;j<n;j++) if(N[j]) M[i][j]+=N[i]*N[j]; }
  }
  P=keepP;
  /* Gaussian elimination; the matrix is small, symmetric and positive definite */
  for(i=0;i<n;i++){ for(j=i+1;j<n;j++){ var f=M[j][i]/M[i][i];
      for(var c=i;c<n;c++) M[j][c]-=f*M[i][c]; rhs[0][j]-=f*rhs[0][i]; rhs[1][j]-=f*rhs[1][i]; } }
  var X=new Array(n), Y=new Array(n);
  for(i=n-1;i>=0;i--){ var sx_=rhs[0][i], sy_=rhs[1][i];
    for(j=i+1;j<n;j++){ sx_-=M[i][j]*X[j]; sy_-=M[i][j]*Y[j]; } X[i]=sx_/M[i][i]; Y[i]=sy_/M[i][i]; }
  var R=[]; for(i=0;i<n;i++) R.push([X[i],Y[i]]); return R;
}

/* the angle the curve turns through at each interior element boundary */
function corners(f){
  var out=[], h=1e-4, d=1e-10;
  for(var k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var a=f(k-1,1-d), a1=f(k-1,1-d-h), a2=f(k-1,1-d-2*h), b=f(k,d), b1=f(k,d+h), b2=f(k,d+2*h);
    var tl=[3*a[0]-4*a1[0]+a2[0], 3*a[1]-4*a1[1]+a2[1]];      /* one-sided, second order */
    var tr=[-3*b[0]+4*b1[0]-b2[0], -3*b[1]+4*b1[1]-b2[1]];
    var gap=Math.hypot(a[0]-b[0],a[1]-b[1]), ang=null;
    if(Math.hypot(tl[0],tl[1])>1e-9 && Math.hypot(tr[0],tr[1])>1e-9)
      ang=Math.abs(Math.atan2(tl[0]*tr[1]-tl[1]*tr[0], tl[0]*tr[0]+tl[1]*tr[1]))*180/Math.PI;
    out.push({k:k, a:a, b:b, gap:gap, ang:ang});
  }
  return out;
}
function curvePath(w,f,e0,e1){
  var d='';
  for(var e=e0;e<e1;e++){ for(var s=0;s<=40;s++){ var q=toSvg(w,f(e,1e-9+(1-2e-9)*s/40));
      d+=(s?'L':'M')+q[0].toFixed(1)+' '+q[1].toFixed(1); } }
  return d;
}
function drawMapPanel(w,f,pts,sel,support,col,other,otherCol){
  var o=PAN[w], s='', i, W=MS*(WX[1]-WX[0]), H=MS*(WY[1]-WY[0]);
  s+='<text x="'+o.x0+'" y="26" font-size="16.5" font-weight="650" fill="'+INK+'">'+o.title+'</text>';
  s+='<rect x="'+o.x0+'" y="'+MT+'" width="'+W+'" height="'+H+'" fill="#fbfcfd" stroke="#e3e7ec"/>';
  if(GHOST) for(var e=0;e<ne;e++)
    s+='<path d="'+curvePath(w,other,e,e+1)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+otherCol+'" stroke-width="2" opacity=".28" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>';
  /* the stretch of curve the highlighted function can move */
  for(e=Math.floor(support[0]);e<Math.ceil(support[1]);e++)
    s+='<path d="'+curvePath(w,f,e,e+1)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="13" opacity=".16" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
  if(w==='B'){                                       /* control polygon */
    var d=''; for(i=0;i<pts.length;i++){ var q=toSvg(w,pts[i]); d+=(i?'L':'M')+q[0].toFixed(1)+' '+q[1].toFixed(1); }
    s+='<path d="'+d+'" fill="none" stroke="#9aa3ae" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>';
  }
  for(e=0;e<ne;e++)
    s+='<path d="'+curvePath(w,f,e,e+1)+'" fill="none" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="3.3" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
  var cs=corners(f), worst=0;
  for(i=0;i<cs.length;i++){
    var c=cs[i], A=toSvg(w,c.a), lab, bad;
    if(c.gap>1e-6){ lab='gap'; bad=true; worst=Infinity; }
    else { var g=(c.ang===null?0:c.ang); worst=Math.max(worst,g); bad=(g>=0.05); lab=g.toFixed(1)+'°'; }
    s+='<circle cx="'+A[0].toFixed(1)+'" cy="'+A[1].toFixed(1)+'" r="4.4" fill="#fff" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.6"/>';
    s+='<text x="'+(A[0]+8).toFixed(1)+'" y="'+(A[1]-11).toFixed(1)+'" font-size="15.5" font-weight="'+(bad?700:500)+
       '" fill="'+(bad?'#b8322a':'#8b95a2')+'" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" paint-order="stroke">'+lab+'</text>';
  }
  for(i=0;i<pts.length;i++){                         /* the points you can drag */
    var q=toSvg(w,pts[i]), on=(i===sel);
    if(w==='L'){
      var vtx=(i%p===0);
      s+='<circle cx="'+q[0].toFixed(1)+'" cy="'+q[1].toFixed(1)+'" r="'+(on?8.5:(vtx?6.5:5.5))+'" fill="'+
         (on||vtx?col:'#fff')+'" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1.8"/>';
    } else {
      var r=on?8:6;
      s+='<rect x="'+(q[0]-r).toFixed(1)+'" y="'+(q[1]-r).toFixed(1)+'" width="'+2*r+'" height="'+2*r+'" fill="'+
         (on?col:'#fff')+'" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="1.8"/>';
    }
    s+='<circle class="grab" data-pt="'+w+':'+i+'" cx="'+q[0].toFixed(1)+'" cy="'+q[1].toFixed(1)+'" r="13" fill="transparent"/>';
  }
  return {svg:s, worst:worst};
}
function drawMap(){
  var U=knots(), fL=ptL, fB=function(e,t){ return ptB(e,t,U); };
  var a=drawMapPanel('L',fL,Q,selL,supportOf('L',selL,U),BLUE,fB,VIO);
  var b=drawMapPanel('B',fB,P,selB,supportOf('B',selB,U),VIO,fL,BLUE);
  mapSvg.innerHTML=a.svg+b.svg;
  function deg(v){ return v===Infinity ? 'a gap' : v.toFixed(1)+'°'; }
  $('bs1_mcap').innerHTML='Each dot on a curve is an element boundary, labelled with the angle the curve turns through '+
    'there. Largest corner: <b>'+deg(a.worst)+'</b> on the Lagrange curve, <b>'+deg(b.worst)+'</b> on the B-spline curve. '+
    'Drag any circle or square. The highlighted point belongs to the highlighted function above, and the shaded '+
    'stretch is the part of the curve it can move.';
}
/* keep the two shapes in step with the bases they belong to */
function syncShapes(){
  var kL=p+'|'+ne, kB=p+'|'+ne+'|'+cont.join(',');
  if(kL!==keyL){ buildL(); keyL=kL; }
  if(kB!==keyB){ buildB(); keyB=kB; }
}
function svgXY(ev){ var pt=mapSvg.createSVGPoint(); pt.x=ev.clientX; pt.y=ev.clientY;
  return pt.matrixTransform(mapSvg.getScreenCTM().inverse()); }
mapSvg.addEventListener('pointerdown',function(ev){
  var t=ev.target.closest('[data-pt]'); if(!t) return;
  var a=t.getAttribute('data-pt').split(':'); drag={w:a[0], i:+a[1]};
  if(drag.w==='L') selL=drag.i; else selB=drag.i;
  draw(); ev.preventDefault();
});
window.addEventListener('pointermove',function(ev){
  if(!drag) return;
  var q=svgXY(ev), z=toPlane(drag.w,q.x,q.y);
  z=[Math.max(WX[0],Math.min(WX[1],z[0])), Math.max(WY[0],Math.min(WY[1],z[1]))];
  if(drag.w==='L') Q[drag.i]=z; else P[drag.i]=z;
  drawMap(); ev.preventDefault();
});
window.addEventListener('pointerup',function(){ drag=null; });
$('bs1_copy').addEventListener('click',function(){
  var U=knots(), f=function(e,t){ return ptB(e,t,U); };
  for(var A=0;A<=ne*p;A++) Q[A]=atXi(f, A/p);
  drawMap();
});
$('bs1_rst').addEventListener('click',function(){ buildL(); buildB(); drawMap(); });
$('bs1_ghost').addEventListener('change',function(){ GHOST=this.checked; drawMap(); });

function reset(){ cont=[]; for(var k=1;k<ne;k++) cont.push(p-1); knot=Math.min(Math.max(1,knot),ne-1);
                  selL=null; selB=null; }
$('bs1_p').addEventListener('input',function(){ p=+this.value; reset(); draw(); });
$('bs1_e').addEventListener('input',function(){ ne=+this.value; knot=Math.floor(ne/2); reset(); draw(); });
/* when the knots change, keep the highlight on the B-spline at the same place:
   the one whose centre (its Greville point) is nearest the old one's */
function centre(U,i){ var s=0; for(var k=1;k<=p;k++) s+=U[i+k]; return s/p; }
function changeKnots(fn){
  syncShapes();                                   /* P belongs to the knots as they are now */
  var U0=knots(), c=(selB===null)?ne/2:centre(U0,selB), cont0=cont.slice(), P0=P.slice();
  fn();
  var U=knots(), nB=U.length-p-1, best=0, d=1e9;
  /* carry the B-spline curve across the change rather than rebuilding it */
  var lower=true, k, Pc=P0;
  for(k=0;k<cont.length;k++) if(cont[k]>cont0[k]) lower=false;
  if(lower){
    var keep=cont; cont=cont0.slice();
    for(k=0;k<keep.length;k++) while(cont[k]>keep[k]){ Pc=insertKnot(knots(),Pc,k+1); cont[k]--; }
    cont=keep;
  } else Pc=refit(U0,P0,U);
  P=Pc; keyB=p+'|'+ne+'|'+cont.join(',');
  for(var i=0;i<nB;i++){ var e=Math.abs(centre(U,i)-c); if(e<d-1e-9){ d=e; best=i; } }
  selB=best; draw();
}
$('bs1_dn').addEventListener('click',function(){ if(cont[knot-1]>-1) changeKnots(function(){ cont[knot-1]--; }); });
$('bs1_up').addEventListener('click',function(){ if(cont[knot-1]<p-1) changeKnots(function(){ cont[knot-1]++; }); });
$('bs1_all0').addEventListener('click',function(){ changeKnots(function(){ cont=cont.map(function(){ return 0; }); }); });
$('bs1_allmax').addEventListener('click',function(){ changeKnots(function(){ cont=cont.map(function(){ return p-1; }); }); });
svg.addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var t=ev.target.closest('.hit'); if(!t) return;
  if(t.hasAttribute('data-k')){ knot=+t.getAttribute('data-k'); draw(); return; }
  if(t.getAttribute('data-w')==='L') selL=+t.getAttribute('data-i'); else selB=+t.getAttribute('data-i');
  draw();
});
reset(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

Things to try:

1. **Support.** With the default settings, click a Lagrange function and then a B-spline function near the middle.
   The shaded band shows where each is nonzero.
   The quadratic B-spline extends across three elements, while a Lagrange function never extends past the elements that touch its node.
2. **Number of functions.** Five quadratic elements require 11 Lagrange functions but only 7 smooth B-splines.
   Each smoothness condition at a boundary removes one function, so the number of B-splines is $p+1$ plus, for each interior boundary, $p$ minus its continuity.
3. **Slopes.** Set the degree to 3 and observe the slope of a B-spline as one boundary is made less smooth.
   The slope is smooth at $C^2$, has a corner at $C^1$, and jumps at $C^0$.
4. **Every boundary $C^0$.** The number of B-splines becomes the number of Lagrange functions.
   The two bases then describe exactly the same set of functions, and on each element the B-splines are the Bernstein polynomials described in the next section.
5. **One boundary at $C^{-1}$.** The B-spline basis separates there into two independent pieces, as if it were two separate patches.
6. **Meaning of a coefficient.** A Lagrange function equals 1 at its own node and 0 at every other node, so its coefficient is the value of the field there.
   Most B-splines never reach 1, and several are nonzero at every point, so a B-spline coefficient is generally not the value of the field at any particular point.
7. **Drag a B-spline control point.** The curve moves smoothly, and only along the shaded part, which is the support of the basis function associated with that point.
   Every boundary still reads 0.0°, since a curve built from $C^1$ functions cannot form a corner, regardless of where its control points are placed.
8. **Drag a Lagrange node.** Its elements move, and corners appear at the neighbouring element boundaries.
   Even before any node is moved, the Lagrange curve has small corners.
   Its nodes lie exactly on a smooth arch, but an arch is not a piecewise quadratic, so the pieces meet at slightly different angles.
9. **Put the Lagrange nodes on the B-spline curve.** Every corner drops to 0.0°, and the two curves become identical.
   The Lagrange functions can represent any curve that the B-splines can represent, but nothing in the Lagrange basis keeps the curve smooth, so moving any node brings the corners back.
10. **Lower one boundary to $C^0$, then to $C^{-1}$.** The B-spline curve does not move.
    Instead, it gains a control point at that boundary.
    Dragging that point allows the B-spline curve to form a corner there or, at $C^{-1}$, to separate.

### Bernstein polynomials

On a single element, the degree-$p$ **Bernstein polynomials**

$$
B_i^p(t)=\binom{p}{i}\,t^i(1-t)^{p-i}, \qquad i=0,\ldots,p, \qquad 0\le t\le 1,
$$

are another basis for the same polynomials as the degree-$p$ Lagrange functions.
Any cubic can be written as a combination of the four cubic Lagrange functions or as a combination of the four cubic Bernstein polynomials.
Only the coefficients change, in the same way that the components of a vector change when the coordinate axes are rotated.

```{python}
#| output: false
fig, bern = C21F.bernstein_figure()
fig_bern_path = save(fig, "C21_Fig7_Bernstein.png")
```

![(a) and (b) The four cubic functions of each basis on one element. Each Lagrange function equals 1 at its own node and 0 at the others, while the Bernstein functions are never negative and sum to 1 everywhere. (c) and (d) One cubic polynomial written in each basis. The Lagrange coefficients $d_i$ are the values of the polynomial at the four nodes. The Bernstein coefficients $c_i$ are the heights of a control polygon; the curve starts and ends on this polygon, and is pulled toward the two interior points without passing through them.](`{python} fig_bern_path`){#fig-c21-bernstein width=86%}

Two properties make Bernstein polynomials useful.
First, they are never negative and they sum to 1, so a curve built from them stays inside its control polygon, which is one reason they are used in CAD.
Second, they are exactly the basis functions of a $C^0$ B-spline: setting every boundary in the widget above to $C^0$ makes the B-splines on each element exactly these polynomials.
This connection, called **Bézier extraction**, allows a spline code to provide each element with a Bernstein basis and a small matrix, and then to assemble element by element in the same loop as a standard finite element code.

### Cubic Hermite polynomials

Splines are one way to obtain $C^1$ continuity.
An older approach, used in beam theory, makes the slope itself an unknown at every node.
The Euler--Bernoulli beam weak form contains second derivatives ($m=2$), so the slope of the deflection must not jump between elements.
A cubic Hermite element uses the deflection $w$ and the rotation $\theta = dw/dx$ at each end,

$$
w^h(t)=h_{00}(t)\,w_1+L\,h_{10}(t)\,\theta_1
       +h_{01}(t)\,w_2+L\,h_{11}(t)\,\theta_2,
\qquad 0\le t\le 1,
$$

where $L$ is the element length and

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_{00}&=2t^3-3t^2+1, & h_{10}&=t^3-2t^2+t,\\
h_{01}&=-2t^3+3t^2,  & h_{11}&=t^3-t^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Neighbouring elements share both $w$ and $\theta$ at their common node, so the deflection is $C^1$.

```{python}
#| output: false
fig, herm = C21F.hermite_figure()
fig_herm_path = save(fig, "C21_Fig8_Hermite.png")
herm_slope = f"{abs(herm['lagrange_slopes'][0]):.3f}"
```

![(a) The four cubic Hermite functions. Two of them are associated with a value at one end, and two with a slope. (b) A beam clamped at both ends under a uniform load (dashed), approximated by two Hermite elements. The two pieces are different cubics, but they share the same deflection and the same slope at the middle node, so the approximation has no corner there. (c) The same beam approximated by two quadratic Lagrange elements through the same nodal deflections. Each element has its own slope at the middle node (+`{python} herm_slope` and −`{python} herm_slope`), so the approximation has a peak where the beam is actually flat.](`{python} fig_herm_path`){#fig-c21-hermite width=100%}

Hermite elements work well for beams and for rectangular plate elements, but they do not extend well to general shapes.
In two and three dimensions, matching slopes across an element edge requires derivative unknowns in several directions at every node, including mixed derivatives, and these only fit together easily on rectangles.
On curved or irregular elements, they become very difficult to match.
Splines obtain their smoothness differently: rather than adding derivative unknowns, each function overlaps several elements.

### From a Class 11 element to a spline patch

In [Class 11](11_Class.qmd), a basis function on a quadrilateral was defined as the product of two one-dimensional functions,

$$
N_A(\xi,\eta)=N_a(\xi)\,N_b(\eta).
$$

A B-spline patch is built in the same way, from one-dimensional B-splines,

$$
R_A(\xi,\eta)=B_a(\xi)\,B_b(\eta).
$$

The difference lies in the support of the one-dimensional factors.
A Lagrange factor is nonzero on one element, or on two if its node lies on an element boundary.
A B-spline factor extends across several elements of the patch.
The widget below shows either basis over the same grid, with the two one-dimensional factors drawn on the back walls as in Class 11.
The dark curves show the function along each element line, which is where a $C^0$ function has a crease.
Drag to rotate the view, and click a dot in the right-hand view to select a function.

Below that, the same functions are again used as a map, this time from the square onto a curved region of the plane, $\underline{x}(\xi,\eta)=\sum_A R_A(\xi,\eta)\,\underline{x}_A$.
The region initially is the quarter annulus of Classes 12, 13, and 20.
The points $\underline{x}_A$ belong to whichever basis is selected at the top of the widget (Lagrange nodes or B-spline control points), and each can be dragged.
Red marks the locations where a grid line forms a corner as it crosses an element line.

```{=html}
<style>
.bs2{--ink:#18202b;--muted:#6b7684;--line:#dfe4ea;--paper:#f8f9fb;max-width:1100px;margin:1rem auto 1.6rem;color:var(--ink)}
.bs2 .bar{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px 24px;align-items:center;padding:10px 14px;
  background:var(--paper);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px;margin-bottom:10px;font-size:13px}
.bs2 .bar b{font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.05em;color:var(--muted)}
.bs2 .bar label{color:var(--muted)}
.bs2 .bar output{display:inline-block;min-width:1.6em;font-weight:600;color:var(--ink)}
.bs2 input[type=range]{width:110px;vertical-align:middle}
.bs2 .seg{display:inline-flex;border:1px solid #c8d0da;border-radius:7px;overflow:hidden}
.bs2 .seg button{font:inherit;font-size:12.5px;padding:4px 12px;border:0;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);cursor:pointer}
.bs2 .seg button+button{border-left:1px solid #c8d0da}
.bs2 .seg button.on{background:#18202b;color:#fff}
.bs2 .pair{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.45fr 1fr;gap:12px}
.bs2 .pair>div{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}
.bs2 .cap{font-size:13px;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.55;margin:9px 2px 0}
.bs2 .cap b{color:var(--ink)}
.bs2 .bar.sub{margin-top:18px}
.bs2 #bs2_map{display:block;width:100%;max-width:660px;margin:0 auto;height:auto;border:1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius:8px;background:#fff;touch-action:none}
.bs2 #bs2_map .grab{cursor:grab}
@media (max-width:820px){.bs2 .pair{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
</style>

<div class="bs2" id="bs2">
  <div class="bar">
    <span class="seg" role="group" aria-label="basis">
      <button type="button" id="bs2_L">Lagrange</button><button type="button" id="bs2_B" class="on">B-spline</button></span>
    <span><label for="bs2_p">degree</label> <input id="bs2_p" type="range" min="1" max="3" value="2">
      <output id="bs2_pv">2</output></span>
    <span><label for="bs2_e">elements per side</label> <input id="bs2_e" type="range" min="2" max="4" value="3">
      <output id="bs2_ev">3</output></span>
    <span id="bs2_cwrap"><label for="bs2_c">spline continuity</label> <input id="bs2_c" type="range" min="0" max="1" value="1">
      <output id="bs2_cv">C¹</output></span>
  </div>
  <div class="pair">
    <div id="bs2_3d" style="height:520px"></div>
    <div id="bs2_top" style="height:520px"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="cap" id="bs2_cap"></div>
  <div class="bar sub">
    <b>THE SAME FUNCTIONS, USED AS A MAP</b>
    <button type="button" id="bs2_copy">put the Lagrange nodes on the B-spline region</button>
    <button type="button" id="bs2_rst">reset both regions</button>
  </div>
  <svg id="bs2_map" viewBox="0 0 660 620" role="img"
       aria-label="The parametric square mapped onto a curved planar region, with points that can be dragged"></svg>
  <div class="cap" id="bs2_mcap"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
'use strict';
var root=document.getElementById('bs2'); if(!root || typeof Plotly==='undefined') return;
var $=function(id){ return root.querySelector('#'+id); };
var C={xi:"#1f5fbf", eta:"#c2410c", node:"#e0a800", ink:"#18202b", grey:"#9aa3ae",
       neg:"#2f6db5", mid:"#f2f2f0", pos:"#b8322a", crease:"#18202b"};
var kind='B', p=2, ne=3, r=1, sel={B:null, L:null};
var SUP={'-':'⁻','0':'⁰','1':'¹','2':'²'};
function Ck(c){ return 'C'+String(c).split('').map(function(q){ return SUP[q]||q; }).join(''); }

/* ---- 1D bases on [0, ne] ------------------------------------------------- */
function knots(){
  var U=[],j,k;
  for(j=0;j<=p;j++) U.push(0);
  for(k=1;k<ne;k++) for(j=0;j<p-r;j++) U.push(k);
  for(j=0;j<=p;j++) U.push(ne);
  return U;
}
function bspl(x,U){
  if(x>=ne) x=ne-1e-12;
  var N=[],i,d,a,b;
  for(i=0;i<U.length-1;i++) N.push(x>=U[i] && x<U[i+1] ? 1 : 0);
  for(d=1;d<=p;d++){
    var M=[];
    for(i=0;i<N.length-1;i++){
      a=U[i+d]>U[i]     ? (x-U[i])/(U[i+d]-U[i])*N[i]           : 0;
      b=U[i+d+1]>U[i+1] ? (U[i+d+1]-x)/(U[i+d+1]-U[i+1])*N[i+1] : 0;
      M.push(a+b);
    }
    N=M;
  }
  return N;
}
function lag(x){
  var n=ne*p+1, out=new Array(n).fill(0);
  var e=Math.min(ne-1,Math.floor(x)), t=x-e;
  for(var a=0;a<=p;a++){
    var v=1; for(var b=0;b<=p;b++) if(b!==a) v*=(t-b/p)/(a/p-b/p);
    out[e*p+a]+=v;
  }
  return out;
}
function basis1D(){ return basisOf(kind); }
function basisOf(kd){
  if(kd==='L'){
    var n=ne*p+1, c=[]; for(var i=0;i<n;i++) c.push(i/p);
    return {n:n, f:lag, centres:c};
  }
  var U=knots(), nb=U.length-p-1, g=[];
  for(var a=0;a<nb;a++){ var s=0; for(var k=1;k<=p;k++) s+=U[a+k]; g.push(s/p); }
  return {n:nb, f:function(x){ return bspl(x,U); }, centres:g, U:U};
}
function support(B,i){
  if(kind==='B') return [B.U[i], B.U[i+p+1]];
  if(i%p===0) return [Math.max(0,i/p-1), Math.min(ne,i/p+1)];
  var e=Math.floor(i/p); return [e,e+1];
}

/* ---- sampling ------------------------------------------------------------ */
function samples(){
  var per=Math.max(10, Math.round(36/ne)), S=[];
  for(var k=0;k<=ne*per;k++) S.push(k/per);
  return S;
}

function render(){
  var B=basis1D(), n=B.n;
  if(sel[kind]===null || sel[kind]>=n*n){
    /* Lagrange: start on an element corner, where four elements meet and the
       crease is the point; splines: start in the middle of the patch */
    var m=(kind==='L') ? p*Math.floor(ne/2) : Math.floor(n/2); sel[kind]=m + n*m;
  }
  var A=sel[kind], i=A%n, j=Math.floor(A/n);
  var S=samples(), Fx=S.map(B.f);
  var fi=Fx.map(function(v){ return v[i]||0; }), fj=Fx.map(function(v){ return v[j]||0; });
  var Z=fj.map(function(b){ return fi.map(function(a){ return a*b; }); });
  var zabs=1e-9; Z.forEach(function(row){ row.forEach(function(v){ zabs=Math.max(zabs,Math.abs(v)); }); });
  zabs=Math.max(zabs, 1);
  var zmin=kind==='L' ? -0.45 : -0.08, top=ne;

  /* the 3D view */
  var T=[{type:'surface', x:S, y:S, z:Z, cmin:-zabs, cmax:zabs, showscale:false, opacity:0.95,
          colorscale:[[0,C.neg],[0.5,C.mid],[1,C.pos]],
          lighting:{ambient:0.75, diffuse:0.5, specular:0.05},
          contours:{x:{show:true, start:0, end:ne, size:0.25, color:'#9aa3ae', width:1},
                    y:{show:true, start:0, end:ne, size:0.25, color:'#9aa3ae', width:1}},
          hovertemplate:'ξ=%{x:.2f}<br>η=%{y:.2f}<br>N=%{z:.3f}<extra></extra>'}];
  /* where the element lines cross the function: a crease for Lagrange, smooth for splines */
  for(var k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var ka=B.f(k), xs=[], ys=[], zs=[], xs2=[], ys2=[], zs2=[];
    for(var q=0;q<S.length;q++){
      xs.push(k); ys.push(S[q]); zs.push((ka[i]||0)*fj[q]);
      xs2.push(S[q]); ys2.push(k); zs2.push(fi[q]*(ka[j]||0));
    }
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:xs, y:ys, z:zs, line:{color:C.crease, width:4},
            hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:xs2, y:ys2, z:zs2, line:{color:C.crease, width:4},
            hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
  }
  /* the element grid on the floor */
  for(k=0;k<=ne;k++){
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:[k,k], y:[0,ne], z:[zmin,zmin], line:{color:'#b8c0ca', width:2},
            hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:[0,ne], y:[k,k], z:[zmin,zmin], line:{color:'#b8c0ca', width:2},
            hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
  }
  /* the two 1D factors on the back walls, as in Class 11 */
  var ones=S.map(function(){ return top; }), zeros=S.map(function(){ return 0; });
  for(var a=0;a<n;a++) if(a!==i)
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:S, y:ones, z:Fx.map(function(v){ return v[a]||0; }),
            line:{color:C.xi, width:2}, opacity:0.22, hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
  for(a=0;a<n;a++) if(a!==j)
    T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:zeros, y:S, z:Fx.map(function(v){ return v[a]||0; }),
            line:{color:C.eta, width:2}, opacity:0.22, hoverinfo:'skip', showlegend:false});
  T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:S, y:ones, z:fi, line:{color:C.xi, width:7},
          name:'1D factor in ξ', hoverinfo:'skip'});
  T.push({type:'scatter3d', mode:'lines', x:zeros, y:S, z:fj, line:{color:C.eta, width:7},
          name:'1D factor in η', hoverinfo:'skip'});
  var lbl=(kind==='L'?'N':'R');
  Plotly.react($('bs2_3d'), T, {
    uirevision:'keep-camera', margin:{l:0,r:0,t:34,b:0},
    title:{text:lbl+'<sub>'+A+'</sub>(ξ,η) = '+(kind==='L'?'N':'B')+'<sub>'+i+'</sub>(ξ) · '+
                (kind==='L'?'N':'B')+'<sub>'+j+'</sub>(η)', font:{size:14}},
    legend:{x:0.02, y:0.98, font:{size:11}},
    scene:{xaxis:{title:'ξ', range:[0,ne], dtick:1}, yaxis:{title:'η', range:[0,ne], dtick:1},
           zaxis:{title:'', range:[zmin, zabs+0.05]}, aspectmode:'manual', aspectratio:{x:1,y:1,z:0.62},
           camera:{eye:{x:-1.45, y:-1.65, z:0.95}}}
  }, {responsive:true, displaylogo:false, displayModeBar:false, scrollZoom:false});

  /* the top-down view: click a centre to pick a function */
  var cx=[], cy=[], cd=[], col=[], sz=[];
  for(var b=0;b<n;b++) for(a=0;a<n;a++){
    var on=(a===i && b===j);
    cx.push(B.centres[a]); cy.push(B.centres[b]); cd.push(a+n*b);
    col.push(on?C.node:C.ink); sz.push(on?15:(n>9?6:8));
  }
  var sp=[support(B,i), support(B,j)], shapes=[];
  shapes.push({type:'rect', x0:sp[0][0], x1:sp[0][1], y0:sp[1][0], y1:sp[1][1],
               line:{color:C.node, width:2.5}, fillcolor:'rgba(0,0,0,0)'});
  for(k=0;k<=ne;k++){
    shapes.push({type:'line', x0:k, x1:k, y0:0, y1:ne, line:{color:'#18202b', width:1}});
    shapes.push({type:'line', x0:0, x1:ne, y0:k, y1:k, line:{color:'#18202b', width:1}});
  }
  Plotly.react($('bs2_top'), [
    {type:'heatmap', x:S, y:S, z:Z, zmin:-zabs, zmax:zabs, zsmooth:'best', showscale:false,
     colorscale:[[0,C.neg],[0.5,C.mid],[1,C.pos]], hoverinfo:'skip'},
    {type:'scatter', mode:'markers', x:cx, y:cy, customdata:cd,
     marker:{size:sz, color:col, line:{color:'#fff', width:1.2}},
     hovertemplate:'function %{customdata}<extra>click to select</extra>'}
  ], {
    margin:{l:42,r:12,t:34,b:40}, showlegend:false, shapes:shapes, dragmode:false,
    title:{text:'seen from above: click a dot', font:{size:14}},
    xaxis:{title:'ξ', range:[-0.12,ne+0.12], dtick:1, zeroline:false, showgrid:false, constrain:'domain', fixedrange:true},
    yaxis:{title:'η', range:[-0.12,ne+0.12], dtick:1, zeroline:false, showgrid:false, scaleanchor:'x', constrain:'domain', fixedrange:true}
  }, {responsive:true, displaylogo:false, displayModeBar:false});

  /* readouts */
  var cells=(sp[0][1]-sp[0][0])*(sp[1][1]-sp[1][0]);
  $('bs2_pv').textContent=p; $('bs2_ev').textContent=ne; $('bs2_cv').textContent=Ck(r);
  $('bs2_L').className=(kind==='L'?'on':''); $('bs2_B').className=(kind==='B'?'on':'');
  $('bs2_cwrap').style.opacity=(kind==='B'?1:0.4); $('bs2_c').disabled=(kind!=='B');
  var nL=ne*p+1, nBs=p+1+(ne-1)*(p-r);
  var lines=(sp[0][1]-sp[0][0]-1)+(sp[1][1]-sp[1][0]-1);
  $('bs2_cap').innerHTML=(kind==='L'
    ? '<b>Lagrange:</b> '+nL+' × '+nL+' = <b>'+(nL*nL)+'</b> functions on these '+ne+'×'+ne+' elements. '+
      'The highlighted one is nonzero on '+cells+' element'+(cells>1?'s':'')+
      (lines>0 ? ', and its surface creases along the element line'+(lines>1?'s':'')+' it crosses (the dark curves).'
               : '. It sits inside a single element and is zero on that element’s edges, so it crosses no'+
                 ' element line; pick a dot on a line to see a crease.')
    : '<b>B-spline, '+Ck(r)+':</b> '+nBs+' × '+nBs+' = <b>'+(nBs*nBs)+'</b> functions on the same '+ne+'×'+ne+
      ' cells (Lagrange would need '+(nL*nL)+'). The highlighted one is nonzero on '+cells+' cells'+
      (r>0?' and crosses the dark curves without a crease.':'; at '+Ck(0)+' it creases along cell lines, as Lagrange does.'))+
    ' The gold box is where the function is nonzero.';
  renderMap();
}

/* ================= the same functions as a map: a curved planar region ==========
   x(xi,eta) = sum_A R_A(xi,eta) x_A, with each x_A a point in the plane.  Each
   basis keeps its own points, so switching basis switches which ones you drag.
   The starting region is the quarter annulus of Classes 12, 13 and 20.         */
var PTS={L:null, B:null}, keyM={L:'', B:''}, drag=null, lastKink=0;
var mapSvg=$('bs2_map'), MW=[-0.32,2.32], MSC=230, MX0=26, MY0=44;
function annulus(s,t){ var r_=1+s, th=Math.PI/2*t; return [r_*Math.cos(th), r_*Math.sin(th)]; }
function build(kd){
  var c=basisOf(kd).centres, n=c.length, P=[];
  for(var i=0;i<n;i++){ P.push([]); for(var j=0;j<n;j++) P[i].push(annulus(c[i]/ne, c[j]/ne)); }
  PTS[kd]=P;
}
function mapAt(Bx,By,P){                      /* sum_ij Bx_i By_j x_ij */
  var x=0, y=0;
  for(var i=0;i<Bx.length;i++) if(Bx[i]) for(var j=0;j<By.length;j++) if(By[j]){
    var w_=Bx[i]*By[j]; x+=w_*P[i][j][0]; y+=w_*P[i][j][1]; }
  return [x,y];
}
function toS(q){ return [MX0+MSC*(q[0]-MW[0]), MY0+MSC*(MW[1]-q[1])]; }
function toP(X,Y){ return [MW[0]+(X-MX0)/MSC, MW[1]-(Y-MY0)/MSC]; }
function pth(pts){ var d=''; for(var i=0;i<pts.length;i++){ var q=toS(pts[i]); d+=(i?'L':'M')+q[0].toFixed(1)+' '+q[1].toFixed(1); } return d; }

/* lowering continuity is knot insertion, so the region does not move */
function insertScalar(U,P,u){
  var k=-1,s=0,i; for(i=0;i<U.length-1;i++) if(U[i]<=u && u<U[i+1]) k=i;
  for(i=0;i<U.length;i++) if(Math.abs(U[i]-u)<1e-12) s++;
  var R=[];
  for(i=0;i<=P.length;i++){
    if(i<=k-p) R.push(P[i]);
    else if(i>=k-s+1) R.push(P[i-1]);
    else { var a=(u-U[i])/(U[i+p]-U[i]); R.push((1-a)*P[i-1]+a*P[i]); }
  }
  var V=U.slice(); V.splice(k+1,0,u);
  return {U:V, P:R};
}
function insertAll(U0,Z0,times){
  var Z=Z0.map(function(r_){ return r_.slice(); }), U=U0.slice(), k, t, j, i, res;
  for(k=1;k<ne;k++) for(t=0;t<times;t++){                     /* along xi: each column */
    var cols=[]; for(j=0;j<Z[0].length;j++){ res=insertScalar(U,Z.map(function(r_){ return r_[j]; }),k); cols.push(res.P); }
    U=res.U; Z=[]; for(i=0;i<cols[0].length;i++){ Z.push([]); for(j=0;j<cols.length;j++) Z[i].push(cols[j][i]); }
  }
  U=U0.slice();
  for(k=1;k<ne;k++) for(t=0;t<times;t++){                     /* along eta: each row */
    var rows=[]; for(i=0;i<Z.length;i++){ res=insertScalar(U,Z[i],k); rows.push(res.P); }
    U=res.U; Z=rows;
  }
  return Z;
}
/* raising continuity cannot keep every region: take the closest smoother one */
function lsq(Bm,v){
  var n=Bm[0].length, M=[], b=[], i, j, q;
  for(i=0;i<n;i++){ M.push(new Array(n).fill(0)); b.push(0); }
  for(q=0;q<Bm.length;q++) for(i=0;i<n;i++) if(Bm[q][i]){ b[i]+=Bm[q][i]*v[q];
    for(j=0;j<n;j++) if(Bm[q][j]) M[i][j]+=Bm[q][i]*Bm[q][j]; }
  for(i=0;i<n;i++) for(j=i+1;j<n;j++){ var f=M[j][i]/M[i][i];
    for(var c=i;c<n;c++) M[j][c]-=f*M[i][c]; b[j]-=f*b[i]; }
  var x=new Array(n); for(i=n-1;i>=0;i--){ var s_=b[i]; for(j=i+1;j<n;j++) s_-=M[i][j]*x[j]; x[i]=s_/M[i][i]; }
  return x;
}
function zAt(Bx,By,Z){ var v=0; for(var i=0;i<Bx.length;i++) if(Bx[i]) for(var j=0;j<By.length;j++) if(By[j]) v+=Bx[i]*Z[i][j]*By[j]; return v; }
function refit(U0,Z0,U1){
  var ts=[], e, s_; for(e=0;e<ne;e++) for(s_=0;s_<8;s_++) ts.push(e+(s_+0.5)/8);
  var B0=ts.map(function(t){ return bspl(t,U0); }), B1=ts.map(function(t){ return bspl(t,U1); });
  var V=ts.map(function(_,a){ return ts.map(function(_,b){ return zAt(B0[a],B0[b],Z0); }); });
  var n1=U1.length-p-1, W=[], i, b;
  for(b=0;b<ts.length;b++) W.push(lsq(B1, ts.map(function(_,a){ return V[a][b]; })));
  var Z=[]; for(i=0;i<n1;i++) Z.push(lsq(B1, W.map(function(w_){ return w_[i]; })));
  return Z;
}
function comp(P,c){ return P.map(function(r_){ return r_.map(function(q){ return q[c]; }); }); }
function zip2(X,Y){ return X.map(function(r_,i){ return r_.map(function(v,j){ return [v, Y[i][j]]; }); }); }

function syncMap(){
  var kL=p+'|'+ne, kB=p+'|'+ne+'|'+r;
  if(keyM.L!==kL){ build('L'); keyM.L=kL; }
  if(keyM.B!==kB){ build('B'); keyM.B=kB; }
}
/* where a grid line crosses an element line, the angle it turns through */
function kinks(kd){
  var f=basisOf(kd).f, P=PTS[kd], h=1e-4, d=1e-9, out={max:0, lines:[]}, k, e, s_;
  var ts=[]; for(e=0;e<ne;e++) for(s_=0;s_<10;s_++) ts.push(e+(s_+0.5)/10);
  var Bt=ts.map(function(t){ return f(t); });
  for(k=1;k<ne;k++){
    var L=[f(k-d),f(k-d-h),f(k-d-2*h)], R=[f(k+d),f(k+d+h),f(k+d+2*h)];
    [0,1].forEach(function(dir){
      var m=dir===0 ? function(Ba,Bb){ return mapAt(Ba,Bb,P); } : function(Ba,Bb){ return mapAt(Bb,Ba,P); };
      var pts=[], bad=[];
      for(var q=0;q<ts.length;q++){
        var a0=m(L[0],Bt[q]), a1=m(L[1],Bt[q]), a2=m(L[2],Bt[q]);
        var b0=m(R[0],Bt[q]), b1=m(R[1],Bt[q]), b2=m(R[2],Bt[q]);
        var tl=[3*a0[0]-4*a1[0]+a2[0], 3*a0[1]-4*a1[1]+a2[1]];
        var tr=[-3*b0[0]+4*b1[0]-b2[0], -3*b0[1]+4*b1[1]-b2[1]];
        var ang=Math.abs(Math.atan2(tl[0]*tr[1]-tl[1]*tr[0], tl[0]*tr[0]+tl[1]*tr[1]))*180/Math.PI;
        out.max=Math.max(out.max,ang); pts.push(a0); bad.push(ang<0.05 ? 0 : (ang<1 ? 1 : 2));
      }
      out.lines.push({pts:pts, bad:bad});
    });
  }
  return out;
}
function renderMap(){
  syncMap();
  var kd=kind, Bs=basisOf(kd), f=Bs.f, P=PTS[kd], n=Bs.n, A=sel[kd], si=A%n, sj=Math.floor(A/n);
  var col=(kd==='L'?'#1f6feb':'#6d28d9'), s='', q, k;
  var per=12, S=[]; for(q=0;q<=ne*per;q++) S.push(q/per);
  var FS=S.map(f);
  function line(dir,c,Fc){ var pts=[];                   /* the image of xi = c (dir 0) or eta = c (dir 1) */
    for(var q_=0;q_<S.length;q_++) pts.push(dir===0 ? mapAt(Fc,FS[q_],P) : mapAt(FS[q_],Fc,P));
    return pts; }
  /* the whole region, and the part where the highlighted function is nonzero */
  var edge=line(1,0,f(0)).concat(line(0,ne,f(ne)), line(1,ne,f(ne)).reverse(), line(0,0,f(0)).reverse());
  s+='<path d="'+pth(edge)+'Z" fill="#f3f6fb" stroke="none"/>';
  var sx=(kd==='B') ? [Bs.U[si],Bs.U[si+p+1]] : lagSupport(si),
      sy=(kd==='B') ? [Bs.U[sj],Bs.U[sj+p+1]] : lagSupport(sj);
  function sub(u0,u1,v0,v1){ var pts=[], m=24, t_;
    for(t_=0;t_<=m;t_++) pts.push(mapAt(f(u0+(u1-u0)*t_/m), f(v0), P));
    for(t_=0;t_<=m;t_++) pts.push(mapAt(f(u1), f(v0+(v1-v0)*t_/m), P));
    for(t_=0;t_<=m;t_++) pts.push(mapAt(f(u1-(u1-u0)*t_/m), f(v1), P));
    for(t_=0;t_<=m;t_++) pts.push(mapAt(f(u0), f(v1-(v1-v0)*t_/m), P));
    return pts; }
  s+='<path d="'+pth(sub(sx[0],sx[1],sy[0],sy[1]))+'Z" fill="'+col+'" fill-opacity=".10" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-opacity=".35" stroke-width="1.2"/>';
  /* grid lines every quarter element, then the element lines over them */
  for(q=1;q<4*ne;q++){ if(q%4===0) continue; var c=q/4, Fc=f(c);
    s+='<path d="'+pth(line(0,c,Fc))+'" fill="none" stroke="#b9c1cc" stroke-width="0.9"/>';
    s+='<path d="'+pth(line(1,c,Fc))+'" fill="none" stroke="#b9c1cc" stroke-width="0.9"/>'; }
  for(k=0;k<=ne;k++){ var Fk=f(Math.min(k,ne));
    s+='<path d="'+pth(line(0,k,Fk))+'" fill="none" stroke="#18202b" stroke-width="'+(k===0||k===ne?2:1.4)+'"/>';
    s+='<path d="'+pth(line(1,k,Fk))+'" fill="none" stroke="#18202b" stroke-width="'+(k===0||k===ne?2:1.4)+'"/>'; }
  /* red where a grid line turns a corner at an element line */
  var kk=kinks(kd); lastKink=kk.max;
  /* small corners (under 1 degree) thin, large ones bold */
  kk.lines.forEach(function(L){
    var run=[], lvl=0;
    function flush(){
      if(run.length>1) s+='<path d="'+pth(run)+'" fill="none" stroke="#d62728" stroke-width="'+(lvl===2?4.5:1.8)+
                          '" stroke-opacity="'+(lvl===2?1:.75)+'" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
      else if(run.length===1){ var z=toS(run[0]); s+='<circle cx="'+z[0]+'" cy="'+z[1]+'" r="'+(lvl===2?2.5:1.4)+'" fill="#d62728"/>'; }
      run=[];
    }
    for(var i=0;i<L.pts.length;i++){
      if(L.bad[i]!==lvl){ flush(); lvl=L.bad[i]; }
      if(lvl>0) run.push(L.pts[i]);
    }
    flush();
  });
  /* the control net (splines), then the points you can drag */
  if(kd==='B'){
    var net='', i, j;
    for(i=0;i<n;i++){ var row=[]; for(j=0;j<n;j++) row.push(P[i][j]); net+=pth(row)+' '; }
    for(j=0;j<n;j++){ var colm=[]; for(i=0;i<n;i++) colm.push(P[i][j]); net+=pth(colm)+' '; }
    s+='<path d="'+net+'" fill="none" stroke="#8b95a2" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>';
  }
  var rr=(n>9?4:5.5);
  for(var b=0;b<n;b++) for(var a=0;a<n;a++){
    var z=toS(P[a][b]), on=(a===si && b===sj), AA=a+n*b;
    if(kd==='B') s+='<rect x="'+(z[0]-(on?7.5:rr))+'" y="'+(z[1]-(on?7.5:rr))+'" width="'+2*(on?7.5:rr)+'" height="'+2*(on?7.5:rr)+
                    '" fill="'+(on?'#e0a800':'#fff')+'" stroke="'+(on?'#18202b':col)+'" stroke-width="1.8"/>';
    else s+='<circle cx="'+z[0].toFixed(1)+'" cy="'+z[1].toFixed(1)+'" r="'+(on?8:rr)+'" fill="'+(on?'#e0a800':col)+
            '" stroke="'+(on?'#18202b':'#fff')+'" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
    s+='<circle class="grab" data-a="'+AA+'" cx="'+z[0].toFixed(1)+'" cy="'+z[1].toFixed(1)+'" r="12" fill="transparent"/>';
  }
  s+='<text x="'+MX0+'" y="26" font-size="17" font-weight="650" fill="#18202b">'+
     (kd==='L'?'Lagrange: the grid passes through its nodes':'B-spline: the region follows its control points')+'</text>';
  mapSvg.innerHTML=s;
  $('bs2_mcap').innerHTML='Largest corner where a grid line crosses an element line: <b>'+lastKink.toFixed(1)+'°</b>'+
    ' (red wherever it is not zero; bold above 1°). Drag any '+(kd==='L'?'node':'control point')+'. The gold one belongs to the '+
    'highlighted function above, and the tinted part of the region is where that function is nonzero, the only '+
    'part that moves. Switch basis at the top of the widget; each basis keeps its own points.';
}
function lagSupport(i){ if(i%p===0) return [Math.max(0,i/p-1), Math.min(ne,i/p+1)]; var e=Math.floor(i/p); return [e,e+1]; }
function changeR(nr){
  syncMap();
  var U0=knots(), r0=r, P0=PTS.B, c=basisOf('B').centres, n0=c.length, A=sel.B===null?0:sel.B;
  var gx=c[A%n0], gy=c[Math.floor(A/n0)];
  r=nr; var U1=knots();
  var fx=(nr<r0) ? function(Z){ return insertAll(U0,Z,r0-nr); } : function(Z){ return refit(U0,Z,U1); };
  PTS.B=zip2(fx(comp(P0,0)), fx(comp(P0,1)));
  keyM.B=p+'|'+ne+'|'+r;
  var c1=basisOf('B').centres, n1=c1.length;
  function near(v){ var b=0,d=1e9; c1.forEach(function(cc,q){ if(Math.abs(cc-v)<d-1e-9){ d=Math.abs(cc-v); b=q; } }); return b; }
  sel.B=near(gx)+n1*near(gy);
}
function svgXY(ev){ var pt=mapSvg.createSVGPoint(); pt.x=ev.clientX; pt.y=ev.clientY;
  return pt.matrixTransform(mapSvg.getScreenCTM().inverse()); }
mapSvg.addEventListener('pointerdown',function(ev){
  var t=ev.target.closest('[data-a]'); if(!t) return;
  drag=+t.getAttribute('data-a'); sel[kind]=drag; render(); ev.preventDefault();
});
window.addEventListener('pointermove',function(ev){
  if(drag===null) return;
  var n=basisOf(kind).n, q=svgXY(ev), z=toP(q.x,q.y);
  z=[Math.max(MW[0],Math.min(MW[1],z[0])), Math.max(MW[0],Math.min(MW[1],z[1]))];
  PTS[kind][drag%n][Math.floor(drag/n)]=z; renderMap(); ev.preventDefault();
});
window.addEventListener('pointerup',function(){ drag=null; });

function switchTo(k){
  if(k===kind) return;
  /* keep roughly the same place on the patch when changing basis */
  var B=basis1D(), n=B.n, A=sel[kind], x=B.centres[A%n], y=B.centres[Math.floor(A/n)];
  kind=k; var B2=basis1D(), m=B2.n;
  function near(v){ var b=0,d=1e9; B2.centres.forEach(function(c,q){ if(Math.abs(c-v)<d){ d=Math.abs(c-v); b=q; } }); return b; }
  sel[kind]=near(x)+m*near(y); render();
}
$('bs2_L').addEventListener('click',function(){ switchTo('L'); });
$('bs2_B').addEventListener('click',function(){ switchTo('B'); });
$('bs2_p').addEventListener('input',function(){ p=+this.value; $('bs2_c').max=p-1; r=Math.min(r,p-1);
  $('bs2_c').value=r; sel={B:null,L:null}; render(); });
$('bs2_e').addEventListener('input',function(){ ne=+this.value; sel={B:null,L:null}; render(); });
$('bs2_c').addEventListener('input',function(){ changeR(+this.value); render(); });
$('bs2_copy').addEventListener('click',function(){
  syncMap(); var B=basisOf('B'), L=basisOf('L'), n=L.n;
  var BL=L.centres.map(function(x){ return B.f(x); });
  for(var a=0;a<n;a++) for(var b=0;b<n;b++) PTS.L[a][b]=mapAt(BL[a],BL[b],PTS.B);
  if(kind!=='L') switchTo('L'); else renderMap();
});
$('bs2_rst').addEventListener('click',function(){ build('L'); build('B'); renderMap(); });
render();
$('bs2_top').on('plotly_click',function(e){
  var pt=e.points.find(function(q){ return q.customdata!==undefined; }); if(!pt) return;
  sel[kind]=pt.customdata; render();
});
})();
</script>
```

Things to try:

1. **A Lagrange corner function** (the default).
   It has creases along both element lines through its node, since each of its one-dimensional factors has a corner there.
2. **Switch to B-spline.** The widget stays at the same location on the patch.
   The B-spline function covers more cells and crosses the dark curves without a crease.
3. **Number of functions.** On $3\times3$ quadratic elements, the Lagrange basis has $7\times7=49$ functions and the $C^1$ B-spline basis has $5\times5=25$, which is the one-dimensional reduction from the previous widget, squared.
4. **Lower the spline continuity to $C^0$.** The number of functions returns to 49, and the creases reappear.
5. **Drag a Lagrange node at an element corner.** The grid lines crossing the neighbouring element lines now form sharp corners there.
   Even before any node is moved, the Lagrange grid has small corners, since its nodes lie exactly on circles and a circle is not a piecewise quadratic.
6. **Switch to B-spline and drag a control point.** The region bends smoothly over a wider area, and no grid line forms a corner.
7. **Put the Lagrange nodes on the B-spline region.** Every corner disappears, since the Lagrange functions can represent exactly the same region.
   However, the Lagrange basis does not keep the region smooth, and moving any node brings the corners back.
8. **Lower the spline continuity to $C^0$.** The region does not move, but control points appear on the element lines, and dragging one of these can now form a corner in the spline grid as well.

A tensor-product spline is defined on a **single** parametric square.
This is well suited to a single CAD surface, such as one flange of the bracket, since mapping the square through $\underline{x}(\xi,\eta)$ places the basis functions on the surface without changing which functions overlap which.
A part made of several surfaces requires several patches glued together, and how well this can be done depends on the layout of the mesh.

## Quadrilateral mesh topology and splines

A tensor-product spline needs a grid that can be indexed by two coordinates, by stepping in either $\xi$ or $\eta$.
A structured quadrilateral mesh has this property, but an arbitrary quadrilateral mesh generally does not.

At a **regular** interior vertex, four quadrilaterals meet.
At an **extraordinary** vertex, a different number meets, such as three, five, or six.
On the boundary, a regular vertex has two quadrilaterals, or one at a corner.
A **separatrix** is obtained by starting at an irregular vertex, following one of its edges into the mesh, and continuing straight through every regular vertex (leaving by the edge opposite the one by which it entered) until reaching the boundary or another irregular vertex.
Cutting the mesh along every separatrix leaves blocks that can each be indexed by two coordinates.
These blocks are the patches that a tensor-product spline would need.

```{python}
#| output: false
fig, sep = C21F.separatrix_figure()
fig_sep_path = save(fig, "C21_Fig9_Separatrices.png")
sep_a_q, sep_a_p = str(sep['a']['nquad']), str(sep['a']['npatch'])
sep_b_q, sep_b_p, sep_b_ev = str(sep['b']['nquad']), str(sep['b']['npatch']), str(sep['b']['n_ev'])
sep_b_val = ", ".join(str(v) for v in sep['b']['valences'][:-1]) + " and " + str(sep['b']['valences'][-1])
sep_c_q, sep_c_p, sep_c_ev = str(sep['c']['nquad']), str(sep['c']['npatch']), str(sep['c']['n_ev'])
sq = lambda k, f: f"{sep[k][f]:.2f}"; sq1 = lambda k, f: f"{sep[k][f]:.1f}"
```

![Three all-quadrilateral meshes of a square plate with a circular hole. Every separatrix was traced using the rule above (violet), and the resulting patches are shaded so that neighbouring patches differ. (a) Four structured blocks around the hole. The only irregular vertices are at the corners of the plate, where two quadrilaterals meet instead of one; their four separatrices divide `{python} sep_a_q` quadrilaterals into `{python} sep_a_p` patches. (b) A mesh built in the way many automatic quadrilateral meshers build one: triangulate, pair neighbouring triangles into quadrilaterals, and then split every element into quadrilaterals. It has `{python} sep_b_ev` interior extraordinary vertices, of valence `{python} sep_b_val`, and its separatrices divide `{python} sep_b_q` quadrilaterals into `{python} sep_b_p` patches. (c) Twelve patches: a ring of four around the hole, four along the sides, and four in the corners. Its `{python} sep_c_ev` extraordinary vertices, all of valence 5, are at the corners of the ring, and their separatrices connect to one another in a loop around the hole, dividing `{python} sep_c_q` quadrilaterals into `{python} sep_c_p` patches.](`{python} fig_sep_path`){#fig-c21-separatrices width=100%}

Mesh (b) is a (moderately) acceptable mesh for standard $C^0$ Lagrange elements.
A Lagrange code only requires neighbouring elements to agree on the values at their shared nodes, and never needs to know which direction is "straight through" a vertex.
Raising the Lagrange polynomial degree does not change this.

Smooth splines are different.
Their functions are intended to extend across element boundaries, and at a valence-3 or valence-5 vertex there is no unique way to continue a row of elements straight through.
Mesh (a) can support four patches of smooth splines, glued along four seams.
Mesh (b) separates into dozens of small patches.
Each seam between patches is a location where continuity must be reduced or specially enforced, so on mesh (b) most of the smoothness that makes splines attractive is lost.
A quadrilateral mesh can therefore be entirely suitable for $C^0$ finite elements and still be a poor starting point for a standard B-spline analysis.

Extraordinary vertices are not problematic in themselves; what matters is how many there are and where they are located.
Mesh (c) has four, placed deliberately at the corners of a ring of quadrilaterals around the hole, and their separatrices connect to one another rather than extending across the plate.
The result is twelve well-structured patches.
This is more seams than mesh (a) has, but they are long and regular, which multi-patch spline codes handle routinely.
The cost is at the four valence-5 vertices, where smoothness must be reduced or specially constructed.
Mesh (c) also has the best elements of the three meshes.

|                                       | (a) four blocks | (b) triangulate, pair, split | (c) twelve patches |
|:--------------------------------------|---------:|---------:|---------:|
| patches                               | `{python} str(sep['a']['npatch'])` | `{python} str(sep['b']['npatch'])` | `{python} str(sep['c']['npatch'])` |
| extraordinary vertices inside         | `{python} str(sep['a']['n_ev'])` | `{python} str(sep['b']['n_ev'])` | `{python} str(sep['c']['n_ev'])` |
| scaled Jacobian of the worst element  | `{python} sq('a','sj_min')` | `{python} sq('b','sj_min')` | `{python} sq('c','sj_min')` |
| average scaled Jacobian               | `{python} sq('a','sj_mean')` | `{python} sq('b','sj_mean')` | `{python} sq('c','sj_mean')` |
| largest edge ratio in one element     | `{python} sq1('a','er_max')` | `{python} sq1('b','er_max')` | `{python} sq1('c','er_max')` |
| largest element's area ÷ smallest     | `{python} sq1('a','size_ratio')` | `{python} sq1('b','size_ratio')` | `{python} sq1('c','size_ratio')` |

: The three plate meshes measured in the same way. {#tbl-c21-plates}

The weakest elements of mesh (a) are at the corners of the plate, where two quadrilaterals share a single right angle and each has a 45° corner.
Smoothing cannot fix this, since it is determined by the layout.
Mesh (c) gives each corner its own block.
Its one weakness is element size: its smallest elements, around the hole, are a few times smaller than its largest, which is a slightly wider spread than in mesh (a).

This is an active area of research.
Constructions such as T-splines, hierarchical and locally refined splines, subdivision surfaces, and spline spaces built specifically around extraordinary vertices all aim to preserve smooth basis functions on meshes with arbitrary layouts.
<!-- For examples, see the work on
[smooth splines on unstructured quad meshes](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2017.06.008),
[blended B-splines on unstructured quad and hex meshes](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2018.07.013),
and [G-spline analysis on arbitrary quadrilateral layouts](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2023.115965).
-->

Note that separatrices describe the topology of a mesh, not its quality.
A well-structured separatrix layout can still produce a poor spline if its cells are folded, highly skewed, or crowded together, just as a Lagrange mesh can.
The separatrices indicate whether a standard tensor-product patch layout is natural, while the quality of the analysis still depends on the Jacobians of Class 13 and on how well the basis can approximate the solution.

## Summary

1. **CAD describes a part as trimmed surfaces glued together.**
   This is an exact description of the shape, but cut cells, slivers, and seams make it difficult to use directly for analysis.
2. **Meshing addresses these problems at the cost of geometric accuracy.**
   A mesh of the trimmed surfaces has no cut cells, but it replaces every curve with straight edges.
3. **Geometry and field have separate roles.**
   IGA uses the same functions for both, but control points place the geometry, while the coefficients $d_A$ are the unknowns of the analysis.
4. **Continuity should be chosen, not maximized.**
   Smoothness is beneficial for smooth solutions and for weak forms with higher derivatives, such as the beam.
   It should be reduced where the solution is not smooth, such as at material interfaces, cracks, and sharp corners.
5. **An exact surface does not define a volume.**
   CAD surfaces can be used directly for shell analysis, but solid analysis still requires a volumetric map or a mesh.
6. **Fewer basis functions does not necessarily mean less computation.**
   Smooth bases can give lower error per unknown, but each function overlaps more elements, so the matrix is less sparse and each element is more expensive to integrate.

Overall, Lagrange finite elements handle complicated geometry well by keeping continuity local, while isogeometric methods invest more effort in geometry and topology so that smooth, CAD-quality basis functions can provide more approximation power across element boundaries.
